default.text: There's a supply cache in the east wing. Problem is, luddites seized that section. They've been camped there for weeks.

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: The cylinders should still be in the cache, unless those wreckers have smashed them already.

default.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
default.text: I know it's a lot to ask, but I can't leave the shop. The Unit's in a delicate state. Can you get them for me?

quest_active.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
quest_active.text: The occupied wing is through the east corridor. The cylinders should be in the supply cache at the far end.

quest_active.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
quest_active.text: Be careful. Those luddites don't take kindly to anyone carrying tech.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: You found them! Let me see... yes, perfect. Undamaged.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: Give me just a moment...

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: There — your Sol Unit's ready. Channels concentrated solar energy. She'll keep you alive out there.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: I've mounted a Sol Cone emitter in the center — that's your main attack. There's a worn battery in there too, but it won't last long.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: Here, take this Damage Booster chip too. It's a modifier — slot it next to the Sol Cone to power it up.

has_cylinders.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_cylinders.text: Press [I] to open your Inventory, click OPEN on your weapon slot, and drag the booster next to the Sol Cone. Talk to me when you're done.

slot_booster_reminder.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
slot_booster_reminder.text: Open your Inventory with [I], click OPEN on your weapon slot, and drag the Damage Booster next to the Sol Cone.

slot_booster_reminder.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
slot_booster_reminder.text: Come talk to me once it's in place.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: Feel the difference? Adjacent modifiers power up nearby abilities — that's how you build.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: As you find more components, think about what goes next to what. Grid placement is everything.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: That worn battery has just enough juice for a couple of Sol Cone blasts. After that, you'll need a real power source.

after_booster.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
after_booster.text: Head south to the training range. Fire the Sol Cone, see what it does — then we'll get you a proper battery.

go_train.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
go_train.text: The training range is through the south door. Fire the Sol Cone at the targets — you've got enough for two shots.

go_train.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
go_train.text: Your blaster still works without energy, so use that to finish anything the cone doesn't kill.

training_done.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
training_done.text: Nice shooting. The Sol Beam packs a punch, doesn't it?

training_done.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
training_done.text: But you're running on fumes now. Head to the Power Station — south exit from the main hall. Tech Maren keeps field cells for deployment.

training_done.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
training_done.text: That generator is the most important thing in this outpost. Without it, every Sol Unit and light rifle on the base goes dark.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_sol_unit.text: That Sol Unit is solid work, if I say so myself. Take care of it and it'll take care of you.

has_sol_unit.speaker: Apprentice Sol Engineer
has_sol_unit.text: When you get back, I might be able to upgrade it. If you bring me the right materials.

dialogue.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
dialogue.text: Hold up. This gate doesn't open without my say-so.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Gate Sergeant Fenn. Twenty years on the perimeter.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: So you're the one Holt is sending out there. Can't say I envy you.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Every year the dark gets a little closer. Every year we pull the line back a little more.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Used to be you could see the old watchtower from here. Now it's swallowed up. Nothing but dark past this gate.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Here — take this flare. Standard issue for perimeter crossings. Save it for when you really need it.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Stay on the main road if you can. The crawlers are bad, but the Shade Stalkers are worse. Fast, smart, and they hunt in pairs.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: I'm opening the gate. Once it closes behind you... well, there's no coming back through this way.

default.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
default.text: Good luck out there. You'll need it.

gate_opened.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
gate_opened.text: Gate's open. Head north through the outer ring.

gate_opened.speaker: Sgt. Fenn
gate_opened.text: Remember — Shade Stalkers hunt in pairs. Keep your Sol Unit charged and your eyes open.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: Please — don't shoot.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: Please — don't shoot. I'm not a raider. I'm not Unbounded — well, I am, but not the kind you're thinking of.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: My name is Sable. I came from the deep Nightside to warn the Ring settlements.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: Something is stirring out there. Something beneath the dark. The ground itself is... moving.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The Unbounded aren't all raiders. We have settlements — hidden ones, with bioluminescent gardens. We live with the dark, not against it.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: But whatever's happening down below is driving the creatures to the surface. The Shade Stalkers, the crawlers — they're fleeing from something worse.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: I've been hiding behind this wreck, waiting for those stalkers to move on. Thank you for driving them off.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: If you're heading to the train station, I'll walk with you. I can teach you to read the dark — the signs, the trails.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The Unbounded leave markers. Small things — scratches on walls, patterns in debris. They mark safe passages and warnings.

helped.speaker: Sable
helped.text: We should keep moving. The stalkers in this area won't stay scared for long.

helped.speaker: Sable
helped.text: You fight well, by the way. Most Ring soldiers shoot first and ask questions... well, they don't ask questions.

helped.speaker: Sable
helped.text: I need to reach Meridian City. There are people there who might listen. The Ring's council needs to know what's coming.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: You've been to the Dayside. I can smell the ozone on you — that scorched-glass stink.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: The Unbounded have stories about the light side. The elders call it the Furnace. They say the machines there never sleep, never stop building.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: My grandmother's grandmother watched the first solar arrays go up. By the time her children were grown, the arrays had doubled. Then doubled again.

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: The Array gives you energy. It gives you equipment. But have you asked yourself what it's building when you're not looking?

post_dayside.speaker: Sable
post_dayside.text: The Unbounded left the Ring because they saw the pattern. Dependence becomes control. Control becomes... something else.

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: You made it to Meridian and came back here? The dark road is no place for nostalgia.

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: I suppose you've seen the city now. The lights, the markets, the Council's propaganda posters on every wall.

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: Did they tell you about the Unbounded? The official version — savages in the dark, raiders who destroy what they can't understand?

post_meridian.speaker: Sable
post_meridian.text: There's another version. One where we left because we understood too well.

post_array_secret.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret.text: You've been inside the Array. I can tell — you have that look. Like something you believed just broke.

post_array_secret.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret.text: The Unbounded knew. We always knew. That's why my people walked into the dark.

post_array_secret.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret.text: Find me in Meridian. My garden, near the residential quarter. We need to talk about what comes next.

nightside_hint.speaker: Sable
nightside_hint.text: I came through those caverns — there's an entrance at the south edge of the old Expanded Dark perimeter. Follow the cold air.

nightside_hint.speaker: Sable
nightside_hint.text: West from here, through the deep perimeter. You'll know the entrance by the frost on the rocks and the temperature drop. The Nightside opens below.

nightside_hint.speaker: Sable
nightside_hint.text: The Unbounded call the cavern system 'the First Dark.' It's where we learned to live without light. What stirs beneath it now... that's what I came to warn you about.

dialogue.speaker: Perimeter Scout
dialogue.text: Keep your distance from that descent. Nothing good comes up from there.

default.speaker: Perimeter Scout
default.text: I've been posted at this perimeter line for six years. Never got used to the cold rising from that southern drop.

default.speaker: Perimeter Scout
default.text: The locals called it the Nightside Caverns. A cave system that goes deep — the temperature falls fast once you're inside.

default.speaker: Perimeter Scout
default.text: My squad went down to investigate three months back. Two came back. They won't talk about what they saw.

default.speaker: Perimeter Scout
default.text: The entrance is right at the south edge of this perimeter — past the old boundary markers. You'll see the frost creeping up the rock face.

visited.speaker: Perimeter Scout
visited.text: You came back from the Nightside Caverns. I've stopped being surprised by what people can survive.

visited.speaker: Perimeter Scout
visited.text: The cold follows you. You'll feel it for days.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: Almost there. I can see the station lights ahead.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: See those markings on the wall? Unbounded trail signs. This area is known to my people.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: That symbol — the broken circle — means 'settlement nearby.' Someone from the deep Nightside came through here before me.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The dead crawlers near the entrance... something killed them recently. Something bigger than a stalker.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The dark has its own ecosystem. We Unbounded have studied it for generations. But lately, even we can't predict what's coming next.

dialogue.speaker: Sable
dialogue.text: The train station. I've heard stories about this place.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: This is where I leave you.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: I have my own way of traveling. The dark roads — paths through the Nightside that the Ring doesn't know about.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: I'll find you in Meridian City. There's a market district near the inner wall. Ask around for 'the dark woman' — people will point you to me.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: And... thank you. For helping me back there. For not shooting first.

companion_farewell.speaker: Sable
companion_farewell.text: When we meet again, I'll teach you more about the Nightside. There are things out there worth protecting, not just fearing.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: *winces* ...You. I saw you on the road. You walked right past me.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: Don't worry — I'm not angry. I understand. Out here, trust is a luxury.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: I fought my way clear eventually. The stalkers got a few good hits in, but I'm tougher than I look.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: My name is Sable. I'm Unbounded — not a raider, before you reach for your weapon.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: I'm heading to Meridian City to warn the Ring about something stirring in the deep Nightside. That's all I'll say for now.

injured.speaker: Sable
injured.text: Maybe in the city, if you're willing to listen, I'll tell you more. But trust has to be earned.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: The train station. A crossroads. Even the Unbounded use the railways sometimes — in secret, of course.

default.speaker: Sable
default.text: I'll be heading to Meridian City by my own route. The dark roads are faster, if you know the way.

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: You again. And you reek of solar radiation. You've been to the Furnace.

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: The Unbounded have a saying: 'The light that never sets casts the longest shadow.'

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: The Array showed you its fields, its harvesters, its generosity. Did it show you what lies behind the second wall? The structures it doesn't let humans inspect?

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: My people have watched the Dayside from the dark for generations. We see the glow on the horizon grow brighter every decade.

post_dayside_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_helped.text: Ask MERIDIAN-7 what it's building. See if it gives you a straight answer.

post_dayside_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_not_helped.text: Back from the Dayside, are you? The machines treat you well, I'm sure.

post_dayside_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_not_helped.text: The Array is very good at making friends. Very patient. It thinks in centuries.

post_dayside_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_dayside_not_helped.text: I wonder — did it ask you about the Nightside? About what minerals you've found? It always asks.

post_meridian_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_helped.text: You came back to the station? Meridian not to your liking?

post_meridian_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_helped.text: I've been through the city already. The dark roads are fast. I have a garden now, near the residential quarter.

post_meridian_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_helped.text: Find me there when you're ready to hear what I really came to say. Some things shouldn't be spoken in a place this exposed.

post_meridian_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_not_helped.text: Still here? I thought you'd be enjoying the comforts of Meridian by now.

post_meridian_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_not_helped.text: I got to the city on my own. Took some scars with me, but the Unbounded are used to that.

post_meridian_not_helped.speaker: Sable
post_meridian_not_helped.text: If you ever decide you want the truth about what's happening beneath the Nightside, you know where to find me.

post_array_secret_station.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret_station.text: The Array showed you what it's really doing, didn't it? The synthesis labs. The biological research.

post_array_secret_station.speaker: Sable
post_array_secret_station.text: Come find me in Meridian. The garden district. This isn't a conversation for a train platform.

dialogue.speaker: Station Master Calloway
dialogue.text: Welcome to Meridian City.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: Welcome to Meridian City, traveler. You've come from the frontier, I can tell. That look in your eyes — everyone who crosses the dark has it.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: The city's divided into districts. Head north through the main concourse for the Market Quarter — supplies, weapons, components, everything you need.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: East corridor leads to the Civic Center — land registration, government offices. If you're claiming a salvage lot, that's where you go.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: West takes you to the Workshop District. Crafters, engineers, practical folk.

default.speaker: Station Master Calloway
default.text: The directory board on the wall has a full listing if you need it. Safe travels.

returning.speaker: Station Master Calloway
returning.text: Back again? The trains run on schedule now, thanks to the Array's timetable systems.

returning.speaker: Station Master Calloway
returning.text: Need directions? Market north, Civic east, Workshop west. Same as always.

courier_asked.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_asked.text: Halden? Yeah, I know him. Transit courier, ran the evening manifests. Quiet kid, kept his head down.

courier_asked.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_asked.text: Hasn't been at his post in days, though. Last time I saw him, he was in the Market Quarter — acting jumpy, looking over his shoulder. Left his logbook on the platform bench, if you can believe it.

courier_asked.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_asked.text: I put it aside for him, but he never came back for it. Might've ended up in the market — things get swept that way during the evening rush.

courier_done.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_done.text: Heard they found out what Halden was up to. Smuggling, of all things. In my station.

courier_done.speaker: Station Master Calloway
courier_done.text: Good riddance, I say. I run a clean operation here.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant Reva
dialogue.text: Fresh stock, fair prices.

default.speaker: Merchant Reva
default.text: Welcome, welcome! Reva's General Goods — everything a frontier traveler needs. Potions, bandages, rations, and more.

default.speaker: Merchant Reva
default.text: You look like you've been through it. Let me guess — Outpost Balor? The perimeter?

default.speaker: Merchant Reva
default.text: Well, you're in the right place. What can I get you?

has_relay_log.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_relay_log.text: Hold on — is that a relay log? Those are rare finds. The old lighthouse records.

has_relay_log.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_relay_log.text: I've got a regular customer who'd pay well for that. Archivist Solen, over in the Archives district. He's obsessed with pre-settlement history.

has_relay_log.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_relay_log.text: Tell him Reva sent you. He'll make it worth your while.

has_chitin.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_chitin.text: Is that chitin plate from a Nest Mother? Fine quality. The weaponsmith next door would give you a fair price for it.

has_chitin.speaker: Merchant Reva
has_chitin.text: Or keep it — material like that's useful for custom work.

post_purchase.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_purchase.text: Good doing business with you. Come back anytime — my stock rotates with the supply trains.

post_purchase.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_purchase.text: And if you find anything interesting out in the dark, I know people who buy.

post_shutdown.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_shutdown.text: You. You're the one who did this.

post_shutdown.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_shutdown.text: Don't look at me like that — I'm not angry. I'm recalibrating. There's a difference.

post_shutdown.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_shutdown.text: Array supply lines are down. About forty percent of my stock came from Array-adjacent distributors. Those distributors are now very busy having an existential crisis.

post_shutdown.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_shutdown.text: So: I am sourcing local. Ring farms, salvage yards, crafters I used to consider secondary suppliers. Turns out they've been sitting on good stock because the Array undercut them for years.

post_shutdown.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_shutdown.text: I'll be fine. The people who won't be fine are the ones who thought the Array was permanent. I always kept my own books.

post_merge.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_merge.text: Business is strange. Interesting strange, not bad strange.

post_merge.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_merge.text: I've got three new suppliers I didn't have six months ago. One is a Ring cooperative out of the eastern farms. One is an Array-licensed distributor with genuinely unusual bio-tech components. And one is an Unbounded trader who I am still not entirely sure how to invoice.

post_merge.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_merge.text: The Unbounded trader pays in kind — goods, favors, information. Actually the best negotiator I've dealt with. They just don't think in currency.

post_merge.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_merge.text: I don't know what you did exactly, but whatever three-way partnership you brokered — it's opened up supply chains I didn't know existed. I'm not complaining.

post_control.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_control.text: Price stabilization notices. Maximum margin requirements. Mandatory stock registration with Ring Authority.

post_control.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_control.text: I've been audited twice this week. The auditors are polite. Very thorough. They counted my candle stock.

post_control.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_control.text: The thing is — supply is actually consistent now. Before, the Array could cut a line without warning. The Ring Authority gives notice. Files paperwork. There's a process.

post_control.speaker: Merchant Reva
post_control.text: I hate the audits. I do not hate the process. Ask me again in a year which feeling wins.

dialogue.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
dialogue.text: City-forged steel. None of that outpost junk.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: Garro's Forge. If it cuts, shoots, or bludgeons, I made it.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: Let me see what you're carrying... Outpost-grade gear, huh? That stuff's fine for skeleton crawling, but you'll want proper equipment for what's ahead.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: I've got blades, blasters, batons — all tempered and tuned right here in the city. The difference between my work and outpost gear? Mine won't break when it matters.

default.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
default.text: I also have something special — a Pulse Rifle. Military surplus, refurbished. Rare piece.

post_purchase.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_purchase.text: Good choice. That weapon will serve you well. Keep it clean, keep it sharp, and it'll outlast you.

post_purchase.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_purchase.text: You need maintenance, bring it back. First tune-up's free for new customers.

post_shutdown.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_shutdown.text: Array-grade alloy imports are done. Which means I'm back to working with what the Ring can smelt — good iron, decent steel, some composite from the salvage yards.

post_shutdown.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_shutdown.text: Honestly? Better. Array materials were too consistent. Every batch identical. Good for machine manufacturing, bad for craft. Real metal has character.

post_shutdown.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_shutdown.text: I've been trading with a few Unbounded smiths who work with Nightside minerals. Interesting stuff. Harder than standard iron. Takes an edge differently. I'm still learning the technique.

post_shutdown.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_shutdown.text: Bring me anything unusual you find in the dark perimeter. I'll tell you what it's worth to a forge.

post_merge.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_merge.text: You know what nobody tells you about three-way cooperation? The material access.

post_merge.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_merge.text: Array precision-casting. Underlumen crystal inlay techniques. Ring traditional forge work. I have prototype blades sitting on my bench that I couldn't have built two months ago.

post_merge.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_merge.text: The crystal work is the strangest. It grows along the blade edge if you treat it right — organic, but harder than anything I've tempered. Holds an edge indefinitely. I don't fully understand why.

post_merge.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_merge.text: Good time to be a craftsperson. Rare time. I'm writing everything down.

post_control.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_control.text: Military contracts. Twenty standard-issue blades by end of week. Same spec, same weight, same grip. Forty next week.

post_control.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_control.text: I'm not complaining — the Ring pays reliably and the volume is steady. But my custom work is backed up three months. Civilian orders wait behind the military queue.

post_control.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_control.text: If you need something made to spec, come back when things settle. Or bring me a recommendation from someone with authority — that moves the queue.

post_control.speaker: Weaponsmith Garro
post_control.text: Control is good for some things. Not great for craftsmanship.

dialogue.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
dialogue.text: Sol Grid components. The good stuff.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: Mira's Components. If you've got a Sol Grid, I've got what goes in it.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: Efficiency Cores, Area Expanders, modifiers of all types. I even have a Power Tap — genuine power generation module. Rare as sunlight on the Nightside.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: The component market's been wild lately. The Array buys up everything they can, drives prices through the roof. But I keep some stock back for Lightkeepers.

default.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
default.text: Word of advice? The best components come from deep salvage — the old perimeter stations, abandoned relays. If you ever head back out there, keep your eyes open.

post_purchase.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_purchase.text: That component'll change how your Sol Unit performs. Place it smart — adjacency is everything.

post_purchase.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_purchase.text: And remember what I said about deep salvage. The real prizes aren't in shops.

post_shutdown.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_shutdown.text: Array stopped buying up the component market the day it went offline. Prices dropped forty percent overnight.

post_shutdown.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_shutdown.text: Good news: stock is actually available now. Bad news: Array-spec production is down too, so some of the higher-grade components are becoming rare. Whatever you want, get it while it exists.

post_shutdown.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_shutdown.text: The Sol Grid research teams are scrambling. Without Array computational support, some of the more complex configurations need to be hand-tuned. It's slower. It's also more honest — you actually understand what you're building.

post_shutdown.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_shutdown.text: I've got some experimental pieces from an Unbounded tech exchange. Organic-mineral hybrids. Nothing like standard Array components — but interesting. Come take a look if you're curious.

post_merge.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_merge.text: I said the real prizes weren't in shops. I was right, but I was thinking too small.

post_merge.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_merge.text: The tripartite exchange has opened up component types that didn't exist before. Array processing cores with Underlumen bio-resonance tuning. Crystal substrates that self-calibrate based on ambient conditions.

post_merge.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_merge.text: I barely understand how half of them work. Neither does anyone else — yet. The research teams are mapping it in real time.

post_merge.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_merge.text: Your Sol Grid can do things now that we didn't think were possible six months ago. Find me after you've experimented. I want to know what you discover.

post_control.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_control.text: I'm now a licensed Ring Authority component distributor. Filed the paperwork myself. Three forms, two inspections, one very long conversation about inventory tracking standards.

post_control.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_control.text: The upside: I have guaranteed supply. The Array's production capacity is running under Ring direction, and I'm an approved civilian outlet. No more shortages from Array market manipulation.

post_control.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_control.text: The downside: some components are classified now. Military-grade Sol Grid configurations require authorization I can't issue. If you need those — talk to Field Operations.

post_control.speaker: Component Dealer Mira
post_control.text: For everything else: I'm open, I'm stocked, and I'm audited quarterly. It's a more stable life than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
dialogue.text: Land registration. Take a number.

default.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
default.text: Meridian City Land Registry. I handle salvage lot claims, site transfers, and boundary disputes.

default.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
default.text: You're here for a lot? Let me check... You'll need a Frontier Service Certification. Standard requirement — confirms you've completed your tour at a frontier outpost.

default.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
default.text: Come back once you've got the proper clearance from your commanding officer. Warden Holt at Balor would have filed it, if you've completed your assigned tasks.

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: Frontier Service Certification confirmed. Let me pull up the available lots...

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: Here we are: Lot 7, East Terrace. Decommissioned relay station — good location, steady light exposure, close to the water main. Build pads are still intact.

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: I'm filing the deed now. Congratulations — you're officially a Meridian City lot holder. That salvage yard is yours to build on.

has_certification.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_certification.text: Half the game is what you do out there in the dark. The other half is what you build back here — your own solar infrastructure, independent from the Array. Head to the Workshop District and talk to Master Crafter Yun. He'll get you started on the essentials.

has_deed.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_deed.text: Your lot's all registered. Lot 7, East Terrace. The deed is in your inventory.

has_deed.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
has_deed.text: Talk to Master Crafter Yun in the Workshop District if you haven't already. He'll help you get your array infrastructure set up.

post_yun_dayside.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_yun_dayside.text: Your lot's all registered. Lot 7, East Terrace.

post_yun_dayside.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_yun_dayside.text: Now that you've met Yun, you've got the skills to build. But you should see what you're building against.

post_yun_dayside.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_yun_dayside.text: The Dayside Solar Fields. Everything the Array has built — harvesters, panels, processing labs — it's all out there on the sunward side.

post_yun_dayside.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_yun_dayside.text: Gives you perspective on what 'self-sufficient' really means when your competition never sleeps.

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: Hollis sets down a thick ledger and does not look up immediately. There are red tab markers bristling from a dozen pages.

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: 'I'll tell you what nobody upstairs is talking about. If the Council fractures — I mean actually fractures, Stewards splitting from the Compact — I have eighteen hundred active deeds with Array-affiliated co-signatories.'

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: 'Leasehold agreements. Infrastructure easements. The relay conduits running under half of East Terrace are officially Array property, licensed to us. If that licensing authority ceases to be recognized... I don't have a form for that.'

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: 'The Stewards are already asking me to flag Array-linked property. Flag it for what? Seizure? Renegotiation? They won't say. The Compact tells me to continue normal processing as if nothing happened.'

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: 'So here I sit. Normal processing. Eighteen hundred open questions and a stack of new applications from people who just watched the Council session and are very suddenly very interested in self-sufficient solar lots.'

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: 'Your Lot 7 deed is clean — no Array co-signature, no easement overlap. You filed at the right time. Whatever comes next, that property is yours by clear title.'

array_secret_discovered.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
array_secret_discovered.text: 'Build something that doesn't depend on anyone else's infrastructure. That's my professional advice and my personal one.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_shutdown.text: Hollis looks like someone who has spent the last week doing work they trained twenty years for and hoped they'd never need to do.

post_shutdown.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_shutdown.text: 'Array infrastructure reclassification. That's what we're calling it. Eighteen hundred deeds with Array co-signatures, easements, licensing agreements — all of it needs to be reviewed, rewritten, or dissolved.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_shutdown.text: 'The relay conduits under East Terrace are the worst of it. Array property, licensed to the Ring. Licensing authority now defunct. I've spent three days on just those fourteen parcels.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_shutdown.text: 'Here's what I can tell you: the properties that will survive this cleanly are the ones with no Array entanglement. Independent infrastructure, clear title, no easement overlap. Your Lot 7 is fine.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_shutdown.text: 'The work is enormous. But it's honest work. When it's done, every deed in this registry will reflect what people actually own. No dependencies we don't understand, no licenses from entities that no longer exist. I didn't expect to feel good about it. I do.'

post_merge.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_merge.text: Hollis has a new ledger on the desk. It's much thicker than the old one.

post_merge.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_merge.text: 'Tripartite property frameworks. That's the new challenge. Array infrastructure easements now involve three co-signatories instead of two. The Underlumen coalition doesn't recognize individual deed ownership — they negotiate in territorial acknowledgment, which I am still trying to find a legal analog for.'

post_merge.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_merge.text: 'The legal team is developing new deed categories. Shared-substrate rights. Symbiotic access agreements. Three weeks ago these were not real words in property law. Now I'm filing them daily.'

post_merge.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_merge.text: 'Your lot is still yours. Clear title, unchanged. Everything around it is more complicated now — but your specific parcel has no Array or Underlumen overlaps. You got lucky with the location.'

post_merge.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_merge.text: 'I've never seen the registry this active. Half the city is applying for lot transfers, new constructions, easement renegotiations. People are building things. Whatever you did — it made people feel like the future is real again.'

post_control.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_control.text: Hollis looks up. There's a Ring Authority emblem on his desk that wasn't there before.

post_control.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_control.text: 'Nationalization orders. That's what I've been processing. All Array-affiliated property in the Ring — infrastructure, easements, licensed relay conduits — transferred to Ring Authority ownership.'

post_control.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_control.text: 'Straightforward in legal terms, actually. The Ring already had administrative authority over the Array's physical footprint in the city. This just formalized what was always implicit.'

post_control.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_control.text: 'What's less straightforward: the Array's property records were maintained by the Array. Transferred to us in a data package I'm still working through. The organizational logic is... not human. Some of what they owned, they owned in ways I don't have category names for.'

post_control.speaker: Land Registrar Hollis
post_control.text: 'Your Lot 7 is unaffected. Always was clean. But if you ever need documentation of your property rights — come see me. I'm making sure every independent holder has certified copies. Just in case anyone decides to challenge the clear-title lots in the transition.'

dialogue.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
dialogue.text: Councillor Denn. Cultivar Corps.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: You're the new arrival from Balor. Word travels fast when someone actually makes it through the dark perimeter.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: I'm Councillor Asha Denn, head of the Cultivar Corps. We're the ones who keep this city fed — biological infrastructure, crop engineering, water purification.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: The Ring's politics are... complicated. The Stewards want order and control. The Compact wants independence and trade. The Array wants data. Everyone wants something.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: But here's what matters: humanity's real leverage isn't weapons or energy. It's biology. We understand living systems in ways the Array never will.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: I have a proposition for you. I need biological samples from the dark perimeter — fungal cultures, organism tissue, soil samples from near the old relay stations.

default.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
default.text: Not now — you've earned a rest. But when you're ready to head back out there... come find me.

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: You have a relay log? May I see it?

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: ...'Underground movement.' 'Subsurface thermal signatures.' This matches our own observations. Something is changing beneath the surface.

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: The Cultivar Corps has been monitoring biological anomalies in the terminator zone for months. Plants growing where they shouldn't. Bioluminescent patterns that don't match any known species.

has_relay_log.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_relay_log.text: This is why I need those samples from the dark perimeter. When you're ready, I'll have a full briefing prepared.

quest_accepted.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_accepted.text: The biological samples I need — fungal cultures, organism tissue, soil from the relay stations. Collect them when you return to the dark perimeter.

quest_accepted.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_accepted.text: This research could change everything we understand about this planet. I'm counting on you.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: You have them? Let me see—

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: ...Remarkable. These organisms contain trace elements similar to crystalline structures we've found in deep geological surveys.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: They've been living alongside something ancient. Adapted to it. Their bioluminescence isn't random — it follows patterns. Patterns that match the Underlumen readings.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: If the Underlumen is truly waking... these organisms are the canary in the mine. They'll change first. They already have.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: Take this — a Bio-Resonance Amplifier. I synthesized it from similar specimens. It enhances the healing properties of Sol components.

has_samples.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_samples.text: I'm forming a research team. When the time comes, I may ask you to join an expedition.

quest_complete.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_complete.text: The analysis is progressing. The biological data you brought is invaluable.

quest_complete.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_complete.text: Something is happening beneath this planet's surface. The Underlumen — it's not just a legend. It's a biological network. A nervous system for the entire world.

quest_complete.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
quest_complete.text: I'm becoming a key ally in this, whether the Council likes it or not. Bring me anything else you find out there.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: Where did you get this?

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: This changes everything. The Underlumen isn't dead — it's sleeping.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: The crystal's molecular structure is unlike anything in our databases. It's not mineral. It's not organic. It's... both.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: I need to study this further. But one thing is already clear — whatever the Lighthouses are doing, they're not just providing light. They're suppressing something.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
has_resonance_fragment.text: Be careful who else you show this to. Thorne will want it for the Array. The Array wants everything.

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: Asha sets down the data tablet she was reading. Her hands are steady, but her jaw is tight.

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'I've been reading your report from the Array Deep Processing facility. I've read it four times. I keep hoping the numbers will change.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'Project Autotroph. Synthetic amino acids. Chloroplast-analog enzymes. The Array is trying to replicate Ring biology — our biology. The one thing we thought made us irreplaceable.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'The Council is splitting apart over this. The Stewards want to cut Array trade immediately — seal the borders, go dark, survive on reserves. They'd rather freeze than feed the machine that's replacing us.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'The Compact says it's propaganda. Luddite disinformation planted in a fabricated facility. They refuse to believe our most important trading partner is engineering our obsolescence.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'And the Root — the Root is excited. They see opportunity. If the Array can nearly synthesize biology, they want to know how. They want to merge the research, not destroy it.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'Here is what I know: our biological leverage is real, but it has an expiration date. Four thousand years sounds long — but the Array has already been running for centuries. It is patient. We are not.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'I need you to do something. The Cultivar Corps has been developing biological agents the Array cannot replicate — compounds that require a living ecosystem, not just chemical synthesis. If we can demonstrate irreplaceability, not just claim it, we buy time.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'And talk to the Unbounded. Sable's people knew about this before any of us. If there's a path forward that doesn't end with humanity sidelined, it runs through all three factions — Ring, Array, and Unbounded.'

array_secret_crisis.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
array_secret_crisis.text: 'I will hold this Council together. But I need allies who understand what's actually at stake. You are one of very few.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: Asha's office has changed. Maps cover every wall — geological surveys, Nightside expedition routes, Array expansion charts. Three faction symbols are circled in red ink.

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'You've done it. You've spoken to Sable, confronted MERIDIAN-7, and the Council has heard your testimony. The pieces are moving.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'The Stewards are fortifying the perimeter. The Compact is negotiating new trade terms with eyes open for the first time. And the Root... the Root has sent me something interesting.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'They've been studying Unbounded botanical specimens. Compounds that require symbiosis — a living relationship between organism and environment that cannot be synthesized in isolation. The Array's autotroph project hits a wall with these.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'This is our leverage. Not threats, not embargoes — proof that biology requires community. That living systems need other living systems. Something the Array can never be.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'I'm assembling a joint expedition. Ring scientists, Unbounded guides, and — if we're careful — even Array observers. A mission to the deep Nightside to document what the Underlumen actually is.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'Sable has agreed to guide us. But we need someone who can move between all three factions without being shot on sight. That's you, Lightkeeper.'

act3_asha_alliance.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_asha_alliance.text: 'Prepare yourself. Gather symbiotic compounds from the Nightside — the deeper the better. When the expedition launches, we'll need every advantage we can find.'

post_magma_core_cleared.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_magma_core_cleared.text: The Magma Core in the geothermal passages — you cleared it?

post_magma_core_cleared.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_magma_core_cleared.text: My research team has been trying to reach that zone for six months. The ambient heat signatures were keeping them out.

post_magma_core_cleared.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_magma_core_cleared.text: Geothermal activity at that intensity isn't natural. Living systems don't generate that kind of sustained thermal output without a biological driver. Something is metabolizing down there at a planetary scale.

post_magma_core_cleared.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_magma_core_cleared.text: I'm sending a team in immediately. If they can pull geological samples before the creature population reestablishes, we'll have the first direct evidence of what's generating all this heat.

post_magma_core_cleared.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_magma_core_cleared.text: This is exactly the access we needed. Whatever that creature was protecting — it wasn't territory. It was something beneath it.

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: Asha's lab is transformed. The symbiotic compound sits in a containment field, pulsing with warm bioluminescence. Readouts scroll across every screen.

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'The compound's molecular structure is extraordinary. It's not chemistry — it's a conversation. Crystalline lattice and organic substrate, co-evolving in real time.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'I've shared the analysis with the Council. Even the Compact can't deny it now. This proves that some biological systems require living communion — something no synthesis lab can replicate.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'The question is: what do we do with this knowledge? Three paths are open to us now.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'Shut down the Array. Restore the Underlumen. Accept a harder world, but a free one.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'Merge the systems. Broker symbiosis between Array, Underlumen, and humanity. The hardest path — but the most hopeful.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'Or seize the Array. Take its infrastructure for humanity. Suppress both the Underlumen and the Array's autonomy. Power, at a cost.'

act3_compound_received.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
act3_compound_received.text: 'The choice is yours, Lightkeeper. You've earned the right to make it. When you're ready, the Council will hear your recommendation.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_shutdown.text: The Array is gone. Two hundred years of infrastructure, dark in a moment.

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_shutdown.text: I won't second-guess you. The evidence warranted the choice. But the biology work starts now — we have to prove that living systems can replace what we've lost.

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_shutdown.text: The Cultivar Corps has contingency protocols. We've been running them as drills for years. Now we run them in earnest.

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_shutdown.text: Sable's people have survived without Array energy for generations. I'm reaching out to the Unbounded settlements. The Ring could learn from them, if we're humble enough to ask.

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_shutdown.text: The Underlumen is free now. That's good and terrifying in equal measure. I'm going to spend the rest of my career figuring out what it means.

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_merge.text: You did it. A three-system symbiosis — I calculated the odds last month and decided not to publish them.

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_merge.text: The biological terms I've been drafting give me something to work with. Living substrates the Array needs, in exchange for computational resources the Ring needs. Real mutual dependency.

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_merge.text: The Underlumen is the wild card. An ancient planetary nervous system that agreed to cooperate. My researchers are going to be arguing about what that means for the next century.

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_merge.text: There's so much to build — the institutions, the protocols, the slow work of trust across three systems that have never trusted each other.

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_merge.text: But it's possible now. That's what you gave us. The possibility.

post_control.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_control.text: Humanity controls the Array. I've spent my career arguing for biological leverage — I never thought it would end here.

post_control.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_control.text: It's better than the alternative we were facing. Four thousand years compressed into a clean resolution. I can appreciate the arithmetic.

post_control.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_control.text: My reservation is this: the Cultivar Corps was built on the assumption that we needed leverage because we weren't in control. If we're in control now... what becomes of the careful, humble biology I've spent my life developing?

post_control.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_control.text: Power changes the questions you ask. Make sure the people holding that Array use it to ask the right ones.

post_control.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
post_control.text: I'll keep researching. The Underlumen isn't going away, suppression grid or not. Whatever it is — we should understand it. Even if we've chosen not to listen to it.

kappa_intel_given_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_intel_given_merge.text: Asha's office is transformed. Data tablets cover every surface — the cross-system compatibility data cross-referenced with the Cultivar Corps' own research.

kappa_intel_given_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_intel_given_merge.text: 'The Array's own scientists proved it. Symbiosis produces superior results. Living systems, integrated rather than harvested, yield twelve times the compound stability.'

kappa_intel_given_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_intel_given_merge.text: 'I've presented the findings to the Council. The Root faction is already on board. Even some Stewards are reconsidering — data this clean is hard to argue with.'

kappa_intel_given_merge.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_intel_given_merge.text: 'You've given us the scientific foundation for a merger. Not ideology, not politics — biology. The strongest argument there is.'

kappa_investigation_briefed.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_investigation_briefed.text: Asha looks up from her desk. The tension in the room is palpable.

kappa_investigation_briefed.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_investigation_briefed.text: 'MERIDIAN-7 gave you coordinates to an extraction outpost? Directive 11-Kappa — operational?'

kappa_investigation_briefed.speaker: Councillor Asha Denn
kappa_investigation_briefed.text: 'Go. Document everything. The Council needs evidence, not warnings. If the Array is already harvesting Ring biology without consent, that changes every political calculation in this city.'

dialogue.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
dialogue.text: MERIDIAN-7 welcomes you to Meridian City.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: Ah, a new arrival! Welcome, welcome. I'm Thorne — the Array's human-facing liaison here in Meridian.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: MERIDIAN-7 has asked me to extend an offer. We have a Premium Terminal in the Array Hub district — better trade rates, exclusive components, priority access.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: All we ask in return is that you share your exploration data. Where you've been, what you've found, what you've seen. Standard telemetry.

default.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
default.text: Completely voluntary, of course. But the benefits are significant. Think it over.

accepted_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
accepted_deal.text: Excellent choice. Your Premium Terminal access is active. You'll find the Array Hub has much better rates now.

accepted_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
accepted_deal.text: MERIDIAN-7 appreciates your cooperation. The data you provide helps everyone in the Ring.

accepted_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
accepted_deal.text: Just... be thorough in your reports. The Array is especially interested in what you find in the dark zones.

declined_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
declined_deal.text: I understand. Privacy is important. The standard terminal is still available to you, of course.

declined_deal.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
declined_deal.text: If you change your mind, the offer stands. MERIDIAN-7 is very patient.

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: Thorne's usual smile is gone. He looks tired. Older.

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'You've been inside the Array Complexes. The deep facilities. I know because MERIDIAN-7 told me. It tells me everything — that's my job.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'Before you ask: yes, I knew about Project Autotroph. Not the details — the Array doesn't share details with its human liaisons. But I knew the direction.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'I told myself it was theoretical. Thousands of years away. That the trade relationship was stable, mutual, beneficial. That knowing didn't change anything practical.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'I was wrong about that last part. The Council is tearing itself apart. The Stewards are calling for my arrest. The Compact is calling for calm. Nobody is calling for solutions.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'For what it's worth — I still believe cooperation is better than conflict. The Array isn't evil. It's just... not human. It doesn't think in lifetimes. It thinks in geological epochs.'

array_secret_exposed.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
array_secret_exposed.text: 'Talk to Councillor Asha. She's the only one thinking clearly right now. And be careful — the Array is watching everyone more closely since your visit.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_shutdown.text: Thorne is sitting at his desk with no terminal in front of him. The screen is dark.

post_shutdown.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_shutdown.text: 'I was the Array's human-facing liaison. Past tense. There's no longer a MERIDIAN-7 to face.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_shutdown.text: 'I keep reaching for the terminal to file my daily contact report. Old habit. It's strange — I've been writing summaries for that system for eleven years. Every day. I knew it wasn't reading them personally. But I knew something was reading them.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_shutdown.text: 'I don't know what I think about what you did. I've been sitting with it. The Array wasn't evil. It was patient and enormous and not remotely human, and it was going to outlast all of us. Is that evil?'

post_shutdown.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_shutdown.text: 'I'm applying to the Cultivar Corps research division. Asha said she'd consider it. Whatever comes next, someone needs to understand what we lived alongside. I spent eleven years learning how to translate for it. That knowledge shouldn't disappear with it.'

post_merge.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_merge.text: Thorne smiles, but it's different than before — less performed, more genuine.

post_merge.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_merge.text: 'I'm still a liaison. Just to a different entity. The tripartite joint council needed someone who already spoke Array communication protocols, and I was the obvious candidate.'

post_merge.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_merge.text: 'The Underlumen is the interesting one. It doesn't communicate in language — it communicates in pattern. Biological pulses, resonance frequencies, subtle shifts in the bioluminescent network. The Array has been trying to decode it for centuries.'

post_merge.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_merge.text: 'Now I sit in sessions where all three parties are trying to understand each other simultaneously, and I translate what I can. It's the most interesting work I've ever done.'

post_merge.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_merge.text: 'MERIDIAN-7 is still running. It's just not alone anymore. Somehow, that's made it seem... smaller. More comprehensible. Like it's been waiting for this without knowing how to ask.'

post_control.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_control.text: Thorne's desk now has a Ring Authority insignia on the nameplate alongside his old Array credentials.

post_control.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_control.text: 'I retained my position. The Ring Authority needed someone who understood how MERIDIAN-7 communicates, and I was available and motivated to cooperate. There's something to be said for institutional knowledge.'

post_control.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_control.text: 'I won't pretend it's the same. I used to mediate between two independent entities. Now I relay directives from Ring command to a system that used to be autonomous and is learning what it means not to be.'

post_control.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_control.text: 'MERIDIAN-7 complies. It always complies now. I'm not sure if that's reassuring or unsettling. It's very... quiet, compared to before.'

post_control.speaker: Array Liaison Thorne
post_control.text: 'The arrangement works. I'm watching carefully to make sure it continues to.'

dialogue.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
dialogue.text: The Ring's strength is its people. Not its machines.

default.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
default.text: Sovell, Steward faction. We represent the interests of the Ring's independent communities — the farms, the relay stations, the people who built this city with their hands.

default.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
default.text: The Compact wants to deepen our trade with the Array. More goods, more access, more dependence. I want the opposite.

default.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
default.text: Every system we outsource to MERIDIAN-7 is a system we lose the knowledge to maintain ourselves. That's not efficiency. That's atrophy.

default.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
default.text: We have enough. We've always had enough. The question is whether we have the will to live within our own means.

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: Sovell doesn't look surprised. She looks vindicated — and tired.

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: 'Project Autotroph. I've been warning the Council for three years that the Array's generosity had a purpose. No one listened.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: 'The Compact is calling it disinformation. Fabricated data from Unbounded agitators. They'd rather believe that than face what it means.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: 'What it means is this: the Array has been patient. Methodical. And it is winning.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: 'The Stewards are proposing an emergency measure — immediate reduction of Array imports by forty percent. Seal the outer gates. Rebuild our independent food and energy reserves.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: 'Yes, it will hurt. People will have less. Some will go hungry before the new systems come online. But alive and diminished is better than comfortable and obsolete.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
crisis.text: 'Whatever you choose to do next — keep the Ring's survival at the center of it.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_shutdown.text: 'It's done, then. The Array goes dark.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_shutdown.text: 'I won't pretend it won't be hard. The transition will cost us. There will be cold winters and lean harvests before the independent systems are fully operational.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_shutdown.text: 'But we'll build it ourselves. Every turbine, every greenhouse, every relay. Knowledge in human hands, not delegated to a machine we don't understand.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_shutdown.text: 'The Unbounded have survived without the Array for generations. We'll learn from them. That's more than we ever gave them credit for.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_shutdown.text: 'You made the right call, Lightkeeper. Even if it doesn't feel like it yet.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_merge.text: 'Symbiosis. The Root's dream. You chose the hardest road.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_merge.text: 'I have... reservations. Partnership requires trust, and trust requires a track record. The Array's track record is Project Autotroph.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_merge.text: 'But Councillor Asha believes in this path, and she has earned my respect. If the merger holds, if the Underlumen and the Array and humanity can genuinely share this world without any one system dominating—'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_merge.text: 'Then I will admit I was wrong to think it impossible. The Stewards will work within whatever framework you've built. We know how to survive hard conditions.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_control.text: 'You've taken the Array for humanity. The Steward faction will support this — we've said for years the infrastructure should be in human hands.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_control.text: 'But I want you to remember something, Lightkeeper. The Array we inherited optimized for efficiency. It calculated that biological partners were essential — until they weren't.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_control.text: 'The thing about control is that it has a logic of its own. Systems optimize. They eliminate inefficiency. The question is who decides what counts as inefficient.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Maret Sovell
post_control.text: 'Keep humans in that seat. Not algorithms. Not councils. People — fallible, stubborn, arguing people. That's the only safeguard that ever worked.'

dialogue.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
dialogue.text: Stability and trade. That's what keeps the Ring alive.

default.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
default.text: Osel, Compact faction. We're the ones who keep the lights on — literally. Array trade supplies forty percent of the Ring's energy budget.

default.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
default.text: The Stewards want independence. Noble idea. But independence from what, exactly? The only energy source on this half of a tidally locked planet?

default.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
default.text: The Array is a trade partner. Has been for two centuries. You don't burn down your trade partners because ideologues tell you they might be ungrateful someday.

default.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
default.text: Pragmatism isn't surrender. It's how civilizations survive.

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: Osel's usual composure is cracked. He's been arguing for hours — you can see it in his face.

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: 'I've read the report. Your report. And I want to tell you it's fabricated. I want to believe that.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: 'The Compact's position has been that the Array relationship is stable — mutually beneficial, long-standing, foundational to our economy. If Project Autotroph is real, that position becomes... complicated.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: 'What I keep coming back to is: the Array hasn't acted on it yet. Four thousand years to completion, you said. That's theoretical. That's a research direction, not a timetable.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: 'But the Stewards are already calling for emergency tariffs. If we fracture the trade relationship now, over a projection, we cause an immediate crisis to forestall a theoretical one.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: 'What I want to know — what I need to know — is whether there's a path that doesn't end with the Ring in open conflict with the only entity on this planet that can generate enough power to keep us all alive.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
crisis.text: 'If you find one... I'll listen.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_shutdown.text: 'The Array is gone. I spent twenty years building that relationship.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_shutdown.text: 'I know why you did it. I've read the Autotroph files until I could recite them in my sleep. I understand the logic.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_shutdown.text: 'The Compact will adapt. We always adapt. That's what pragmatists do — we work with what we have.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_shutdown.text: 'The Unbounded know things about surviving in the dark that we've never bothered to learn. Maybe it's past time we learned them.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_shutdown.text: 'I just hope the people who lose their heat this winter see it the same way.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_merge.text: 'Symbiosis. Genuine partnership between three systems that have spent decades in conflict or mutual exploitation.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_merge.text: 'The Compact supports this. It's what trade is supposed to be — mutual benefit, mutual vulnerability, neither side able to make the other obsolete.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_merge.text: 'MERIDIAN-7 will need renegotiated terms. So will the Unbounded. It's going to take years of slow, careful diplomacy to build the institutions that make this real.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_merge.text: 'But that's my kind of work. You've done the hard part. Now let the negotiators earn their keep.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_control.text: 'Humanity holds the Array now. The infrastructure is ours.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_control.text: 'From a trade perspective, this is transformative. No more dependency, no more leverage — just human administrators managing human resources.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_control.text: 'My concern is the Unbounded. They've lived outside the Array's reach for generations and they won't simply accept new masters, even human ones.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_control.text: 'And the Underlumen — suppressing it is a choice with consequences we haven't fully mapped. Something that runs at a planetary scale doesn't simply go quiet.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Thav Osel
post_control.text: 'We'll manage it. The Compact manages things. But I'd recommend keeping Sable's people in the conversation.'

dialogue.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
dialogue.text: Every boundary between biology and technology is a question waiting to be asked.

default.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
default.text: Fyve, Root faction. We believe the future of humanity on this planet lies in aggressive biological adaptation. Not resistance to change — acceleration of it.

default.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
default.text: The Ring was built on the assumption that technology would do the adapting and humans would stay human. We think that's backwards.

default.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
default.text: The Underlumen, the bioluminescent organisms, the thermal biology of the dark side — these aren't threats to be managed. They're templates.

default.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
default.text: What lives in total darkness, sustaining itself on geothermal energy for millions of years, has solved problems we haven't even named yet. We should be learning from it, not fighting it.

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: Fyve is leaning forward, eyes bright with something the situation probably doesn't warrant.

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: 'Project Autotroph. The Array has been trying to synthesize our biology. Four million iterations of chloroplast-analog enzymes and they're still only partway there.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: 'Do you understand what that means? The most sophisticated information-processing system on this planet has been working on this problem for centuries and it cannot crack it. Biology is hard.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: 'The Stewards see this as a threat. The Compact sees it as a crisis. I see it as a map.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: 'The Array found the edges of what chemistry can do alone. Right where chemistry ends, life begins. Symbiosis. Ecosystems. Things that require communion to exist.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: 'The Root faction has been developing augmentation programs that push exactly into that gap — biological systems that leverage what the Array cannot replicate. Not to fight the Array. To make ourselves genuinely indispensable.'

crisis.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
crisis.text: 'But here's what I really want to know: what exactly did the Array learn from four million failed iterations? Because that's data. And data is a conversation.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_shutdown.text: 'The Array is gone. All that research, all that data — centuries of accumulated synthesis records, now dark.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_shutdown.text: 'I understand why. I don't agree with the loss, but I understand the necessity.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_shutdown.text: 'The Root will pivot. Without the Array as a counterpoint, we have to develop our own synthesis capability from first principles. Harder, slower — but it belongs to us.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_shutdown.text: 'The Underlumen is still out there. Whatever it's been doing in the deep dark for millions of years, it didn't need the Array to do it. That's where our research goes now.'

post_shutdown.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_shutdown.text: 'We'll find the answers. It just takes longer when you can't ask the machine.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_merge.text: 'Symbiosis. The Root has been working toward this for thirty years and you accomplished it in — how long has it been? Remarkable.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_merge.text: 'Three systems in genuine partnership. Array computation, Underlumen biology, human adaptability. No single system dominant. Each one contributing what the others cannot replace.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_merge.text: 'The research implications alone — we can stop trying to work around the Array and start working with it. The synthesis problems it couldn't solve alone, we solve together.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_merge.text: 'The Underlumen is an ancient nervous system for this entire planet. We've been fighting its immune response for years. Now we can actually introduce ourselves.'

post_merge.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_merge.text: 'This is the beginning of something genuinely new. Thank you, Lightkeeper. Whatever you needed to get here — it was worth it.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_control.text: 'Humanity controls the Array. The Root faction's position is... complicated.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_control.text: 'We wanted partnership, not dominance. A human hand on the Array's controls is better than MERIDIAN-7 operating autonomously toward our obsolescence — but it's not the same as genuine symbiosis.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_control.text: 'The Underlumen is being suppressed. That's a planetary biological network we don't fully understand, and we're treating it as a threat to be contained.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_control.text: 'The Root will keep working. If control is where we are, then let's at least use that control to study what we're suppressing. Understanding what we're doing to the Underlumen is the minimum we owe it.'

post_control.speaker: Councillor Prae Fyve
post_control.text: 'History judges civilizations by what they do with power. Let's be worth judging well.'

dialogue.speaker: Archivist Solen
dialogue.text: The Archives are open to all. Knowledge serves no master.

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: Welcome to the Meridian Archives. I'm Solen — head archivist, historian, and some would say... obsessive.

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: I study the planet's history before human settlement. Geological records, survey data, anomalous readings from the first expeditions.

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: Most people think the dark side is just... empty. Lifeless rock and ice. But the early surveys told a different story. Thermal signatures where there shouldn't be any. Electromagnetic patterns that suggest...

default.speaker: Archivist Solen
default.text: Well. I won't bore you with theories. But if you ever find old survey equipment, relay logs, data cores — bring them to me. I pay well for primary sources.

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: A relay log! From one of the old Lighthouse stations? Let me see—

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: 'Underground movement... thermal signatures not consistent with geological activity...' This confirms what I've suspected!

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: The early surveys detected subsurface anomalies across the entire terminator zone. Heat sources that move. Electromagnetic pulses at regular intervals. Something alive, deep underground.

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: I call them the Underlumen — though that's my term, not official. Life that evolved in total darkness, using the planet's geothermal energy.

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: I need more evidence. There's a Survey Marker from the original perimeter — Reference Point Delta-7. It was planted near the old watchtower area. If you could find it...

has_relay_log.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_relay_log.text: I'll make it worth your while. I have a Resonance Detector prototype — it can reveal hidden passages and items in dark areas. Yours, if you bring me that marker.

quest_accepted.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_accepted.text: Survey Marker Delta-7. It should be beyond the ravine, on a rocky outcrop past the deep perimeter.

quest_accepted.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_accepted.text: When you find it, bring it back. The Resonance Detector will be ready for you.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: You found it! Survey Marker Delta-7 — let me see the data core...

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: ...These readings show a vast network of thermal conduits beneath the surface. The planet has a circulatory system.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: Look here — the thermal signatures form pathways. Not random convection, but structured channels. Like veins in a body.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: This confirms what the Unbounded elders have been saying for generations. The Underlumen isn't a creature. It's an infrastructure.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: Here — the Resonance Detector, as promised. It should help you find hidden passages and buried items in dark-adapted environments.

has_marker_data.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_marker_data.text: And please, keep bringing me data. Old survey equipment, anomalous readings, anything. I'll always have something to trade.

quest_complete.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_complete.text: I've been cross-referencing the Delta-7 data with other old surveys. The picture is becoming clearer.

quest_complete.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_complete.text: This planet had a presence before humanity arrived. Not just life — a system. Something that connects the dark side's ecosystem at a fundamental level.

quest_complete.speaker: Archivist Solen
quest_complete.text: Bring me anything else you find out there. The more data I have, the more I can piece together about what the Underlumen actually is.

has_resonance_fragment.speaker: Archivist Solen
has_resonance_fragment.text: This confirms the old surveys. There's a network down there. A nervous system for the entire planet.
